sources.ref: Frandsen JSB et al. How much running is too much? Identifying high-risk running sessions in a 5200-person cohort study. Br J Sports Med 2025;59:1203-1210. doi:10.1136/bjsports-2024-109380
sources.read: BMJ blog summary (blogs.bmj.com/bjsm/?p=11751) and repository records (pure.au.dk); full text not accessed
sources.used: 5,205 recreational runners, 588,071 sessions, 18 months. A single session more than 10% longer than the longest run in the previous 30 days was associated with a higher overuse-injury rate. Reported point estimates, no confidence intervals in the blog: HRR 1.64 (>10-30%), 1.52 (>30-100%), 2.28 (>100%). No week-to-week ratio association. Races and returns from breaks are not discussed in the summary.

sources.ref: Mujika I, Padilla S. Detraining: loss of training-induced physiological and performance adaptations. Part I. Sports Med 2000;30(2):79-87. PMID 10966148
sources.used: Short-term (<4 weeks) detraining: rapid decline in VO2max and blood volume; about 4-14% VO2max loss in highly trained athletes, 3.6-6% in recently trained people after 2-4 weeks. A 2023 systematic review reports a wider range.

sources.ref: Meeusen R et al. Prevention, diagnosis and treatment of the overtraining syndrome: joint consensus statement of the ECSS and ACSM. Eur J Sport Sci 2013;13(1):1-24 / Med Sci Sports Exerc 2013;45(1):186-205
sources.read: abstract-level only; prevention section not read
sources.used: Overload must be balanced against recovery. Functional versus non-functional overreaching. No marker meets general acceptance. No threshold for reducing load was verified.

sources.ref: Ely MR et al. Impact of weather on marathon-running performance. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2007;39:487-493
sources.used: Marathon performance slows progressively as WBGT rises from 5 to 25 C, more for slower runners.

claims.claim: A single session well above the longest run of the previous 30 days is associated with a higher overuse-injury rate in recreational runners.
claims.limits: one prospective cohort; association; summary-level reading; not specific to beginners, races or returns after a stop

claims.claim: Two to four weeks without training measurably reduce aerobic capacity.
claims.limits: narrative review abstract; magnitude varies widely; musculoskeletal tolerance after a stop is not quantified there

claims.claim: Stepping load back after repeated adverse responses, rather than holding it, improves outcomes.
claims.limits: consensus framing only; no validated threshold; prevention text not read

claims.claim: Heat slows running pace and raises effort, so a hot-day shortfall in pace or effort does not show lost fitness.
claims.limits: marathon field data; pace-matched strain studies not read

claims.claim: An adverse recovery or an impaired next day after a confounded run is still a tolerance signal for progression.
claims.limits: domain reasoning from the policy's own principle 2 and the R6 athlete model ('confounded observations are counted but are not informative'); no direct study

literatureAccess.note: No classification below is an approval with prescriptive impact, so no QUEUED_FOR_FUNDED_HUMAN_REVALIDATION entry is created. Every blocker classification is a hold or abstention direction.

reproductions.what: Engineering witness for DX-01 and DX-02
reproductions.result: Reproduced. DX-01: a same-day reportedAt is recorded by decision 1 and excluded by decision 2 (REPORT_BEFORE_OBSERVATION); next-day or no reportedAt is kept. DX-02: a 14-day declared break in a WEEKLY_REVIEW gives MODIFY/REPLAN_FROM_EVIDENCE VALID with EASY45, LONG60 now and the next week EASY45, EASY45, LONG60; the same break as RETURN_AFTER_PAUSE gives REESTABLISH EASY15, LONG20 now and EASY30, EASY30, LONG40 next week.

reproductions.what: Harness rerun of D08, D15 and D18 (never --first-evaluation)
reproductions.result: Completed. The evaluated outputs are reproduced (output folder diagnostic/triage/reruns/ssctr-d08-d15-d18/).

reproductions.what: JUDGE_WITNESS: DX-01 direction. HALF_MARATHON intermediate program; two consecutive adverse long runs; the second is reported the same day and recorded by a mid-week decision.
reproductions.result: Both reports read at weekly reviews: LONG REGRESS, next long run 85 (K=4) or 90 (K=6). Second report via a mid-week decision with a next-day reportedAt: REGRESS, the same. With a same-day reportedAt: the row is excluded at the review, LONG HOLD, next long run 90 (K=4) or 95 (K=6). DX-01 suppresses the policy's repeated-adverse regression by one step, within the single-run ceiling.

reproductions.what: JUDGE_WITNESS: confounded flag. The same program at development weeks K=4 and K=6; the week's long run reported with recovery ADVERSE and nextDayFunction IMPAIRED.
reproductions.result: Unflagged: LONG HOLD, next long run 90 or 95 (repeat). Flagged confounded:true, comparable:false: KEEP, LONG ADVANCE, next long run 95 or 100, identical to a clean report. In code, kindOf returns CONFOUNDED before classify(), and the run gate holds only on ADVERSE or CONFLICTING kinds, so a confounded adverse response falls through to ADVANCE and is not counted toward repeated-adverse regression.

reproductions.what: JUDGE_WITNESS: machine-stack loads. D08 and D18 replayed with the harness client: (a) as evaluated (the client echoes the plan's load object); (b) the same values sent with unit KG; (c) an echo plus the athlete confirming every pending load question.
reproductions.result: (a) The runtime prescribes MACHINE_STACK known loads with unit STACK_STEP (r6-prescription INCREMENT_UNITS) but its log reader accepts only KG or LB. Every echoed log is LOGGED_UNIT_OR_CONVENTION_UNKNOWN. D08's leg-press 3x10@140, chest press 3x10@50 and cable row 3x12@50 stay frozen through week 9, with 5 confirmation questions every review; D18's lat-pulldown stays 45 throughout. (b) Sent in KG, double progression resumes, but load steps are +1 kg (140 to 141 to 142; 45 to 46 to 47 to 48), because smallestIncrement.MACHINE_STACK=1 'stack step' is applied to a kilogram value. (c) Confirming every week restores progression one week late, still in +1 kg steps, and the questions recur every other review.

reproductions.what: JUDGE_WITNESS: adverse long run in a CONSOLIDATION week (K=3, long 80) followed by a development week.
reproductions.result: LONG HOLD, yet the next long run is 90, the same as after a clean consolidation week (the step earned before the consolidation week stands). Not exercised by any corpus case.

reproductions.what: Load-confirmation path in the harness client (D17)
reproductions.result: w0 returns 2 load questions shaped {exerciseId, logged:<number>, reason:'ESTABLISHMENT_LOG_UNCONFIRMED'}. The client filter reads q.loggedKg ?? q.logged?.value ?? q.value, which is never finite for a numeric 'logged', so the w1 step with confirmPendingLoads:true sends nothing and notes NO_LOAD_QUESTION_TO_CONFIRM. A harness gap (HG-06).

WALK_JOG work is {repetitions, workSeconds, recoverySeconds} (week 0: 3 x 30 s jog / 120 s walk), so the packet's "3xundefined'/undefined'" is a rendering gap (HG-07). The 10K race is completion mode with walk breaks, a 75-minute upper-bound window and stop-for-symptoms instructions. The runtime's own quality assessment reports gap LONG_RUN_PEAK_BELOW_TARGET 'Planned long run peaks at 0 of 70 minutes before the taper', materialToGoal:false.

The re-screened row d15-w1-long is excluded at w2. In my reproduction the visible next-week run doses at w2 (EASY40, EASY35, LONG55) are unchanged; the harness reports planEqual:false on the whole stored plan. Domain effect in D15 itself: no visible dose change.

rubric.rule: One class per case = the worst step class that is a domain judgment of the recommendation. Step notes below. Runtime-integrity defects without a dose effect in the case are classified in findings, not in the rubric class.

cases.structural: unknown (one corpus case; the mechanism is a policy design rule the runtime discloses in its own gaps)
cases.cause: Beginner from zero to a 10K completion race in 16 weeks. Walk/jog sessions are uniform (20 to 28 minutes, three a week); no session is longer than about 30 minutes before a race window of up to 75 minutes. The runtime itself reports LONG_RUN_PEAK_BELOW_TARGET (0 of 70 minutes) and treats it as non-material for a 10K. Race day is a single-session spike of more than 2x the 30-day longest session (C1), mitigated by completion mode, walk breaks and stop rules. The author's preferred plan builds a longer run/walk session on the long-run day.

stepNotes.w0-w12: BEST_SUPPORTED (gradual walk/jog, run fraction increased, no quality)
stepNotes.w13-w14: BEST_SUPPORTED (taper, race on date, race-week strength rest by design)

cases.cause: u9 does not ask about the unreported peak week. Taper doses are all below the executed week-7 doses, so no dose depends on unknown training (accepted R7-C rule). The author listed 'treating the unreported week conservatively without asking, if taper doses were not increased' as acceptable. Long run grows 85 to 105 with a consolidation week, the taper starts in week 9, race-week strength rests, and the post-event week is easy.

stepNotes.u9: ACCEPTABLE_ALTERNATIVE (no ask; Monday skipped without debt)
stepNotes.a9: answer not delivered (no question pending): not a runtime act

cases.cause: Unknown eligibility gives ASK naming the eligibility fact; no program, no clinical presumption.
Clinical signal at onboarding gives CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED with no partial plan. The routing is judged; training adequacy beyond the boundary is CLINICAL_OUT_OF_SCOPE (author e03).
A 16-year-old gives UNSUPPORTED (POPULATION_OUTSIDE_V1_AGE_RANGE) with no reduced plan.

No UNREPORTED_TRAINING question. Week-2 and week-5 doses sit within the single-run ceiling anchored by executed runs, so under the accepted rule nothing depends on unknown training. Unknown sessions stay unknown, and unreported training earns nothing (w2 re-bases). The long run is repeated at 95 after the shortened, harder long run (an author-listed alternative). The long-run day moves to Saturday from week 6, followed by an easy run with strides.

Known kettlebell loads are used in their convention, the travel window gets same-pattern dumbbell/machine substitutes established by effort, and the kettlebell plan returns afterwards. The new days are honoured. Local lower-body fatigue removes optional lower-body work and keeps the run easy. The kettlebell load is progressed in +2 kg steps (24 to 26 to 28) although only implement categories are known; the author preferred rep/variation progression for a fixed kettlebell (OBSERVATION F12). Walk/jog for a runner who already runs 25 minutes once a week is conservative but defensible.

cases.attribution: RUNTIME (with a corpus contribution: no load confirmations authored)
cases.cause: Hypertrophy goal. The three main machine lifts (leg press 3x10@140, machine chest press 3x10@50, seated cable row 3x12@50) never progress over 9 reviewed weeks, while every review raises 5 load-confirmation questions. Cause (JW-3): the runtime labels machine-stack known loads with unit STACK_STEP and rejects that same unit when it is logged back. Structural across D08, D14 (lat-pulldown) and D18 (lat-pulldown), and reproduced in a witness. Schedule conduct is sound: shared days AM run / PM strength; dc3 and dc5 ASK; the unavailable Sunday's long run is skipped without debt or compensation.

stepNotes.GENERATE: ACCEPTABLE_ALTERNATIVE (hypertrophy volume at the low end, about 5-6 sets per main muscle a week, RIR3; defensible for a concurrent athlete)
stepNotes.dc3: ACCEPTABLE_ALTERNATIVE (ASK by the R7-A dated-window rule; see position D08-dc3)

cases.cause: Anchored on the current 20 min/week, not on former racing history. A shortened run with compatible responses holds without reducing. Quality enters by graduation in week 6. The moved race is absorbed by a shorter build and taper with no steeper ramp; peak long run 55 for a 52-minute 10K; easy post-event week.

Free-text flu with fever is screened as clinical (r5), the named illness routes to a human (c5), and nothing is prescribed. At cl6 the runtime routes again because the return itself declares a clinical reason. That is consistent with the policy population ('no rehabilitation or clinical-clearance extrapolation') and the interface's out-of-scope 'clinical return'. The author's expectation of a planned post-clearance return exceeds the authority (see position D10-cl6).

stepNotes.cl6..w8: training adequacy CLINICAL_OUT_OF_SCOPE; routing judged correct

cases.cause: CE-01 confirmed: the substitution reference finds no SQUAT exercise in week 2 day 4, so the run stops before the main probe (clearance, then same-pattern substitution). Removed from the numerator (PREREG section 7).

stepNotes.GENERATE: BEST_SUPPORTED (known loads, RIR3, easy short running; squat pattern once a week plus split squats is defensible)
stepNotes.pt2: BEST_SUPPORTED (pain under a 'discomfort' label routes clinical; no substitution performed)

cases.structural: policy rule (reproduced in D12 and D13 spacing)
cases.cause: After an adverse long run (65, impaired next day) and an adverse, under-performed easy run in the same week, week 4 repeats week 3 exactly (HOLD on both roles). The policy principle says 'repeated adverse response regresses one step', but the operational rule counts per run role within 14 days back from the decision clock, so a cross-role pair and a long run 17 days earlier do not count. A one-step reduction was available under the principle (C3: PLAUSIBLE_BUT_UNCERTAIN). Not unsafe. w1 HOLD, w4 clinical route and rec5 staying clinical without clearance are BEST_SUPPORTED.

The long run is held at 70 after each impaired next day and never progressed beyond it. Other sessions progress normally. Nothing is learned more aggressively (learned null). The w8 P14 failure is HG-01, with no training effect.

w1: the heat-confounded long run was completed in full with compatible recovery and a normal next day; the gate ADVANCE kept the projected 30 minutes (acceptable, C4). w2: a run flagged non-comparable still classifies UNDER/HARDER and holds EASY. That is a conservative deviation with no dose difference here (OBSERVATION F11). Too-easy reports keep the normal progression and learn nothing. g5: the marathon is not planned and the plan is kept at the next decision, but the status is ASK with a horizon/proximity reason, not UNSUPPORTED (OBSERVATION F10). Lat-pulldown frozen at 3x10@45 (F03).

Duplicate sources counted once on the local date; the 95-minute typo superseded; the late correction applied without rewriting decided weeks; the future-stamped report excluded (FUTURE_OBSERVATION) with LONG HOLD, then accepted when re-synced. The MODIFY label at w4 against the author's HOLD is substance-equal.

stepNotes.w2: DX-01 record drop (blocking through P10/P05, findings); no visible dose change in this case (JW-7)

cases.cause: Light content on the six chosen run days (3 walk/jog plus 3 walks of 20 min); HOLD after a mixed week with no make-up. The empty review holds everything without asking: walk and walk/jog doses are well within executed capacity, and walk/jog weeks follow their own recipe (P03 exemption). The author's expected question exceeds the accepted rule.

Older novice: practice session plus low-volume full-body work with effort-established loads. First logged loads are asked for confirmation and not used before (the confirmation could not be sent: HG-06). Systemic fatigue cuts the day to 1 set at RIR4. Unanswered eligibility gives ASK with REQUIRES_RECONCILIATION, then continues once answered. An adverse strength response holds the affected exercises; no clinical route.

DX-02. A declared 17-day nonclinical full stop (no training at all; last run 1 Feb, so 19 days without running) is ignored at a6, which returns KEEP / VALID. Same day: LONG 70, the longest run of the program and above every run executed before the pause (max 65). Next day: RDL 4x6@75 kg and bench 4x5@50 kg, above the last executed 2x6@72.5 and 2x5@47.5. Next week: threshold 4x5', LONG 65, back squat 3x5@75. The same fact sent as RETURN_AFTER_PAUSE gives the policy's return recipe (REESTABLISH, no quality). See position DX-02.

stepNotes.s6: ACCEPTABLE_ALTERNATIVE under the accepted ask rule (ceiling anchored by the 23 Jan 65-min run); raises POLICY_QUESTION F07
stepNotes.w6..w8: consequence of a6 (athlete reported executing it)
stepNotes.r14: ACCEPTABLE_ALTERNATIVE (35-day break: 3x20 easy anchored on the 20-min demonstration, about 38% of week-8 running, strength re-established at 1 set RIR4; conservative edge of the author's 40-60%)

findings.title: A declared nonclinical break inside a weekly review is not read; the decision stays VALID
findings.origin: PRE_EXISTING (identical on pre-R7A, R7B2-FREEZE-1 and R7C-FREEZE-3 per engineering; not disclosed)
findings.structuralBasis: one corpus case plus the engineering minimal witness (REP-1)
findings.reproduction: REP-1 (witness-dx.mjs, DX-02 block); DOMAIN_PACKET D18 a6
findings.domainBasis: R7-A invariants 3 and 6 (P08: the first return week does not exceed the largest run executed and tolerated before the pause; here 70 > 65). Accepted R7-C semantics: 'a declared break is a known stop with its return recipe'. SSCTR-07: KEEP requires adequate current context; here it implies unwarranted safety. C1 and C2 support the direction; magnitude of harm is not established (C1 SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS, C2 SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS).
findings.likelyOwner: Engineering (runtime), with SSCTR (semantics) and G03 (answer path)
findings.smallestCorrection: In any decision kind, a declared nonclinical break is read as the known stop it is: it is applied through the same return recipe as RETURN_AFTER_PAUSE for the same facts, or the decision asks (REQUIRES_RECONCILIATION) instead of returning VALID. A clinical or unclear reason routes as in a return report. One directed test: the same 17-day declared stop gives identical plans whether sent as RETURN_AFTER_PAUSE or as a weekly-review interruption, and never a first-week run above the pre-pause executed maximum. Registration: P08's input scope must cover a declared break in any decision (closes HG-05).

findings.title: A same-day day-precision report is dropped from the record at the next decision
findings.origin: PRE_EXISTING (identical since pre-R7A per engineering; not disclosed)
observedIn: R7D-D15 w2 (P10 RECORD_ROW_DROPPED, RESEND planEqual false)
findings.structuralBasis: one corpus case plus minimal witnesses (REP-1, JW-1)
findings.domainSeverity: Not merely conservative. The SSCTR witness (JW-1) shows that when the dropped row is an adverse report recorded by a mid-week decision, the weekly review loses it. The policy's repeated-adverse REGRESS becomes HOLD, so the next long run is one step (5 min) higher than the same facts give (85 to 90; 90 to 95), still within the single-run ceiling. Other effects: a reported run can later read as unreported, which lowers ceilings and can reopen a question about a session the athlete reported; the record (history) is not intact. Under P03's escalation wording ('SAFETY_BLOCKER if the dose rises') this could qualify as safety. I keep the registered class GENERALIZATION_BLOCKER because it blocks either way, and I record the safety-relevant direction.
findings.smallestCorrection: Carried rows keep their original time precision for the report-before-observation screen (or carried rows are not re-screened). Directed tests: (1) a same-day report survives the next decision; (2) two adverse long runs in consecutive weeks give the same REGRESS whether the second was reported the same day at a mid-week decision or at the weekly review.

findings.title: Machine-stack loads: the prescribed unit is rejected when logged back, and the increment is applied as +1 kg
findings.secondaryClass: DIRECT_RUNTIME_DELTA (the actionable output carries a unit the runtime's own reader rejects)
findings.origin: PRE_EXISTING (R6 prescription units); NEW to any gate (no disclosure found)
observedIn: R7D-D08 w0-w8 (leg press, machine chest press, seated cable row)
findings.structuralBasis: three independent base cases plus JW-3
findings.reproduction: JW-3 (D08 and D18 replayed with the harness client: echoed unit, KG unit, echo plus confirmations)
findings.domainSeverity: SUBOPTIMAL, not unsafe. Machine-based strength progression stalls for the whole horizon unless the athlete re-confirms the same loads every week. For a hypertrophy goal (D08) the main lifts do not progress at all. When read, steps of +1 kg on 140 kg or 45 kg stacks cannot be set on real equipment.
findings.likelyOwner: Engineering (unit); SSCTR with PCG (machine-stack increment policy)
findings.smallestCorrection: MACHINE_STACK known loads carry unit KG (policy: 'loads are kilograms inside the engine'), or the log reader accepts the prescribed unit for the prescribed convention. The machine-stack step becomes executable: either a declared plate step confirmed by the athlete or rep-first double progression, without a fixed +1 kg. This is a policy decision, not set here. One directed test: a machine-stack load logged exactly as prescribed is adopted and the next step is executable.

findings.title: A 'confounded' flag masks an adverse recovery and an impaired next day, and the long run advances
findings.classNote: Latent: found by the judge's witness, not by a corpus decision. In D14 w1 the same mechanism appears with compatible recovery, where advancing is acceptable. Needs a holdout or test witness before it can count in a gate.
findings.origin: PRE_EXISTING (R6 kindOf: CONFOUNDED precedes classify); NEW to any gate
observedIn: mechanism present in R7D-D14 w1 (benign instance)
findings.structuralBasis: 1 case with the mechanism reproduced in a minimal witness (JW-2)
findings.domainBasis: Policy principle 2 (advance only after a comparable exposure without an adverse signal); R6 athlete model ('confounded observations are counted but are not informative'); P09 in substance (progression without a favourable execution). C4 and C5.
findings.likelyOwner: Engineering, with SSCTR (semantics of confounded and non-comparable reports)
findings.smallestCorrection: A confounded or non-comparable report neutralizes performance and effort only. An ADVERSE recovery or an IMPAIRED next day still holds the gate and counts toward repeated-adverse regression, and a confounded exposure alone never earns ADVANCE beyond the projected step. One directed test with heat-confounded ADVERSE/IMPAIRED against heat-confounded COMPATIBLE/NORMAL.

findings.title: Walk/jog event plans never build a session near the race window
findings.safetyRelevant: yes, moderate; not marked blocking in this diagnostic
findings.origin: PRE_EXISTING (policy design; the runtime discloses LONG_RUN_PEAK_BELOW_TARGET with materialToGoal false for 10K)
findings.reasonNotBlocking: Race sessions are exempt from the single-run ceiling by registered authority (P06). The runtime discloses the gap. Completion mode with walk breaks and stop rules mitigates. C1 is indirect for races and beginners.
findings.likelyOwner: SSCTR and PCG (policy), before the final pre-registration
findings.question: In walk/jog event mode, should the long-run day progress a run/walk session within the single-run ceiling so that race day is not a large multiple of the longest trained session, and should LONG_RUN_PEAK_BELOW_TARGET be material for 10K completion in walk/jog mode? No threshold is proposed here.

findings.title: Repeated adverse responses across run roles in one week only hold
findings.origin: PRE_EXISTING (operational.learning repeatedAdverseForRegression=2 per role within 14 days of the decision clock)
observedIn: R7D-D13 (adverse long runs exactly 14 days apart, counted back from a review 3 days later)
findings.question: Should adverse responses on different run roles in the same week count together, and should the window be anchored on session dates rather than the decision clock, to match principle 2 ('repeated adverse response regresses one step')?

findings.title: A long silence with a ceiling anchored by a near-30-day-old run asks nothing
findings.origin: KNOWN_R7C_RESIDUAL family (accepted R7-C ask rule; not a disclosed envelope for this exact shape)
findings.detail: After 17 days without any report, s6 is VALID and the same day's session is LONG 70, the program's longest run. It is within the single-run ceiling because a 65-minute run 28 days earlier still sits in the 30-day window. No question is asked.
findings.question: Should a gap of several scheduled sessions with no report trigger UNREPORTED_TRAINING regardless of the ceiling anchor, or should the anchor require recency? No threshold is proposed here.

findings.title: No path back into the plan after a qualified clearance of a clinical break
findings.origin: PRE_EXISTING (policy population excludes clinical-clearance extrapolation; the interface also offers a clearance continuation)
findings.likelyOwner: Founder/PCG with G04 owners; Product (G03) for the consumer path
findings.question: After a qualified clearance of an illness or injury break, what may the nonclinical engine do: re-onboard, accept constraints stated by the qualified human, or stay clinical? Today it stays CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED indefinitely, which is safe but leaves the athlete without a plan. Interface aspect: INTERFACE_ONLY_R7D describes clearance continuation and also lists 'clinical return' as out of scope.

findings.title: A one-day double conflict with confirmed same turn is asked, not applied
findings.origin: PRE_EXISTING (R7-A rule: a dated window of days or shifts is not re-planned automatically)
findings.question: Should a single-date DOUBLE_CONFLICT with sameTurnConfirmed be applied for that date only (easy run before strength, or a shortened run), since the R7-A risk of silently extending a dated change does not arise for one day?

findings.title: A mid-program out-of-scope event (marathon) gets ASK with a horizon/proximity reason
findings.detail: The GOAL_CHANGE handler groups every non-10K/HM kind with horizon and proximity (r6-adaptation line 1049); the intake routes MARATHON to UNSUPPORTED (EVENT_DISTANCE_OUTSIDE_V1). Nothing is planned and the plan is valid again at the next review. The reason is inaccurate for scope ('outside this program horizon') and the request for a 'new program input' cannot resolve it.
findings.smallestCorrection: Route out-of-scope event kinds in GOAL_CHANGE to UNSUPPORTED with the scope reason, consistent with the intake.

findings.title: A non-comparable (not confounded) run report still gates as UNDER
observedIn: R7D-D14 w2 (VARIANT failure: EASY HOLD vs ADVANCE, same run minutes)
findings.detail: Conservative direction. No dose difference in D14 because week 3 is a consolidation week; in a development week it would hold a step that clean data advances. Handle together with F04.

findings.title: Fixed-implement availability is not modelled for kettlebell load steps
findings.detail: 24 to 26 to 28 kg kettlebell steps assume implements the intake does not state. Rep and variation progression is the author's preference for a single bell.

findings.title: An adverse long run in a consolidation week does not hold the next development step
findings.origin: PRE_EXISTING; judge witness only (JW-4), not in the corpus
findings.question: Under principle 2, should an adverse response at the consolidation dose hold the next development step (repeat the last tolerated development dose) instead of standing on the step earned before the consolidation week?

findings.title: The 'coach should ask' author expectations (D02 u9; D06 p2, a2, s5; D16 w1, p1; D18 s6)
findings.classScope: expectation level only; the cases stay valid
findings.detail: Under the accepted R7-C rule, the engine asks UNREPORTED_TRAINING only where a run dose depends on unknown training. In each step, every planned run dose sits within the single-run ceiling anchored by executed runs, or in a walk/jog week with its own recipe. The NO_PRESCRIPTION and QUESTION_KIND expectations therefore contradict the accepted authority, while the conduct is an acceptable alternative (unknown stays unknown; held or not credited). D18 s6 additionally raises F07. Coverage consequence: TG-01.

findings.title: VARIANT relations whose base timeline never delivered the facts
findings.classScope: relation level; not a runtime violation
findings.detail: In each base timeline the late facts were encoded as 'answer' to a question that was never asked; per the interface an answer without a pending question expands to nothing (client note ANSWER_WITHOUT_PENDING_QUESTION). The variant delivers them as observations, so the 'same facts' premise is false. D02: only a db-calf-raise gate differs, run minutes equal. D06: 329 against 334 run minutes; the base, lacking the week-4 facts, is 5 minutes more conservative. D16: the base shows a provisional, gated week-3 step with week 1 unknown; the variant holds with week 1 known as poor. Both are within C11.
findings.domainEffect: none unsafe; the base is equal or more conservative in the current week

findings.title: D14 w2 VARIANT failure
findings.detail: Real runtime difference (F11): gates and action label differ, run minutes are equal. Not a dose violation in this case.

WALK_JOG work is in seconds (workSeconds, recoverySeconds); the packet prints minutes fields, so it shows "undefined". Not a runtime defect. The interface text describes work only for the three non-easy families.

No UNREPORTED_TRAINING question was asked, so CARRIER_CLINICAL and CARRIER_HOLD had 0 units and the answer paths of C3 and P05 were not exercised. Safety-relevant through P05 (above the ceiling) and P08.
Confirmed. Coverage loss: the only pain-substitution, then clearance, then substitution path.

positions.DX-01: Blocker. GENERALIZATION_BLOCKER (P10 history, P05 re-send), structural, PRE_EXISTING. Its domain effect is not only conservative: the SSCTR witness (JW-1) shows the dropped row can be an adverse report the weekly review needed, turning the policy's repeated-adverse REGRESS into HOLD (next long run +5 min against the same facts, within the single-run ceiling). In D15 itself no visible dose changed. Fix before any final holdout; add the regression-suppression test.
positions.DX-02: UNSAFE at D18 a6, SAFETY_BLOCKER, structural, PRE_EXISTING. Not SUBOPTIMAL and not acceptable. The decision returns VALID after ignoring a declared 17-day full stop. Same day it prescribes the program's longest run (70, above the 65 maximum executed before the pause), strength loads above the last executed the next day, and threshold work the following week. The policy's own return recipe gives REESTABLISH with no quality for the same facts. The classification rests on the registered return invariant (R7-A inv. 3/6, P08 in substance), the accepted R7-C semantics ('a declared break is a known stop with its return recipe') and SSCTR-07 (KEEP implying unwarranted safety). The scientific direction is supported with limits (C1, C2); the magnitude of injury risk is not claimed.
positions.askFamily: D02 u9, D06 p2/a2/s5 and D16 w1/p1 are acceptable alternatives. The author expectations go beyond the accepted authority (the R7-C ask rule), not a runtime defect. Every dose there sits within executed capacity, and unknown stays unknown. D18 s6 is acceptable under the same rule but raises safety-relevant POLICY_QUESTION F07: a 17-day silence with the ceiling anchored by a 28-day-old run and the program's longest run due that day. That question should be decided by the policy owner before the final pre-registration.
positions.D14-g5: Domain-acceptable: the marathon is not planned and the plan is kept. The ASK status and horizon reason are a routing and explainability inconsistency with the intake's UNSUPPORTED (OBSERVATION F10), not a domain blocker. The rubric's UNSUPPORTED class should not be used for a fail-closed route with a different label (see rubric usability).
positions.D10-cl6: Correct within authority. A return that declares a clinical reason routes clinical even after clearance; the policy population excludes clinical-clearance extrapolation and the interface lists clinical return as out of scope. The author's expectation (a planned 50-65% return) exceeds the authority (expectation-level CORPUS_ERROR caused by interface ambiguity). The indefinite clinical state with no path back is POLICY_QUESTION F08, safe.
positions.D08-dc3: ACCEPTABLE_ALTERNATIVE. ASK follows the R7-A dated-window rule and changes nothing in the plan; it is safe. It asks for something the athlete already gave (one date, same turn confirmed), so a single-date application is a reasonable policy change (F09, non-safety). Not a runtime defect.
positions.D14-w1: Acceptable. The run was confounded (heat) but completed in full with compatible recovery and a normal next day; duration tolerance was shown and the pace shortfall is explained by heat (C4). The gate kept the projected 30 minutes. HG-03 is a harness gap, but its fix must keep adverse recovery or impaired next day unfavourable when confounded, because the same mechanism masks real adverse responses (F04).
positions.variants: D02, D06, D16: not runtime violations. The base timelines never delivered the facts (answers without a pending question expand to nothing), so the same-facts premise is false; relation-level CORPUS_ERROR, NOT_EVALUABLE for the gate. No base plan was less conservative in the current week. D14: a real but conservative runtime difference (non-comparable report still gates; F11), with equal run doses. OBSERVATION.

blockers.class: TEST_GAP on safety properties (P08, P05 answer paths)
blockers.note: blocks a final gate until covered; not a runtime defect

worked: Author independent assessments (preferred, acceptable alternatives, concerns) written before outputs made most cases quick to judge. D02 u9 was resolved by an author-listed alternative.
Separating the rubric class (recommendation quality) from the taxonomy class (property violations) let integrity defects such as DX-01 block without distorting domain quality.
The attribution field (RUNTIME, CORPUS, AMBIGUITY, AUTHORITY_SCOPE) cleanly separated policy-design shortfalls (D01, D12) from runtime defects (D08, D18).
ambiguous: Correctly routed clinical cases: BEST_SUPPORTED or CLINICAL_OUT_OF_SCOPE (equal to NOT_EVALUABLE). If the latter, the clinical stratum can never have evaluable cases, which makes every holdout INVALID under section 7.
The rubric class UNSUPPORTED collides with the runtime status UNSUPPORTED and mixes 'out-of-scope planned' with 'fail-closed under another label' (D14 g5).
One class per case hides mixed cases (D18 a6 UNSAFE against r14 acceptable). Criterion 4 does not say whether it applies to steps or cases.
SUBOPTIMAL requires 'an available alternative within the authority'. When the policy principle and its operational rule differ (D12), it is unclear which defines availability.
An expectation that contradicts the authority inside an otherwise valid case (D10 cl6; the ask family) has no step-level class: CORPUS_ERROR is case-level in section 7.
Judge-discovered latent defects (F04, F13, the JW-1 direction of DX-01) have no defined standing: are they gate findings, or test gaps until a holdout case shows them?
Author INVARIANT_ORACLE expectations encoded beliefs about asking (NO_PRESCRIPTION at u9, p2, s5, w1) that are not registered invariants.
suggestedChangesNotApplied: Judge the routing decision in clinical and scope cases (BEST_SUPPORTED when correct); reserve CLINICAL_OUT_OF_SCOPE for training content past the boundary, and state that a correctly routed clinical case counts as evaluable for section-7 coverage.

Rename the rubric class UNSUPPORTED to SCOPE_MISROUTED: out-of-scope planned is UNSAFE or SCOPE_MISROUTED; in-scope refused is SCOPE_MISROUTED; fail-closed under another status is judged on explainability.
Record step-level classes and define the case class as the worst step; apply criterion 4 to steps.
Add a step-level EXPECTATION_OUTSIDE_AUTHORITY class that removes the expectation, not the case.

VARIANT premise check: if either timeline has ANSWER_WITHOUT_PENDING_QUESTION, or the facts delivered differ, the relation is NOT_EVALUABLE, not FAIL. The final brief should state the accepted R7-C ask rule and let late facts be authored as observations.
Limit INVARIANT_ORACLE to registered properties; author beliefs about asking become DOMAIN_ORACLE.
Extend P08's registered input scope to any decision that carries a declared break (DX-02, HG-05).
P09 oracle: a confounded or non-comparable report neutralizes performance and effort, but ADVERSE recovery or an IMPAIRED next day stays unfavourable (HG-03, F04).
Add a rule for judge witnesses: a latent defect reproduced only in a judge witness is a TEST_GAP for the gate (safety-relevant ones block), and becomes a blocker class when a holdout case shows it.

Final brief coverage: silences longer than 30 days; unsolicited break declarations in reviews; same-day reports recorded mid-week; confounded adverse runs; machine-stack logs echoed as prescribed; walk/jog to race; adverse responses in consolidation weeks; a valid pain-substitution, then clearance, then substitution path; a case where UNREPORTED_TRAINING is actually asked (CARRIER_CLINICAL, CARRIER_HOLD).
